wiki-iran.standing: Wikipedia's article on Iran, and how many people read it each day. Attention to a country's reference page rises when that country is doing something the rest of the world has to price in — a war, a closure, a negotiation.
wiki-iran.recent: The strait is the story. Iran's Supreme National Security Council keeps the Strait of Hormuz closed until Washington "corrects its behavior", and on 8 August added compensation for war damage to its conditions — a demand no executive waiver can satisfy. Transits are down a third; Oman is brokering, and Trump halted a planned attack on 2 August.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is priced against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser prices move after it.
brent.recent: Brent has fallen from its May high as the Strait of Hormuz closure settled into a known quantity rather than a shock: crude from Iraq now moves overland through Syria, and Trump halted the attack on Iran's infrastructure on 2 August. The floor came 2 July, before Iran set six conditions for reopening and the Senate moved to tax buyers of Russian oil.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of West Texas Intermediate, the light sweet crude that sets the US benchmark and prices most North American oil. It moves on supply and policy, and fuel, freight and plastics move after it.
wti.recent: Crude fell 4.5% after a remark on Iran drained the war premium, and a treasury secretary's Hormuz deal claim reversed the gains that followed. OPEC+ then hiked output by 188,000 barrels daily, leaving the price near $82 despite Ukrainian strikes on two Russian refineries.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, settled at a Louisiana pipeline junction and used to price most American gas contracts. It sets what power plants, factories and heating bills pay, and it moves on weather, storage and how much gas leaves the country as LNG.
natgas-hh.recent: Gas has drifted down through the summer, from $3.34 on May 29 to a low of $2.58 on Jul 29, with the supply shocks in the coverage landing on other markets: the drone strikes on LNG vessels at Egypt's Damietta port and the Bulgaria pipeline blast hit European and Mediterranean routes, not US supply. Domestic demand news ran the other way, with SpaceX building its own natural gas power plants for a Texas chip factory.

wheat.standing: The world price of milling wheat, the grain that becomes bread and flour for most of humanity. It moves on harvests, export policy and freight, and governments that subsidise bread absorb the difference or pass it to the street.
wheat.recent: The FAO price index hit 131.1 as heatwaves and wars pushed crop costs to a three-year high. The strain shows downstream: a 20kg flour bag in Karachi now costs Rs3,000 after an import tender delay, Punjab farmers blocked roads on August 7, and Egypt is rewiring how 64 million people pay for subsidised bread.

rice.standing: The world benchmark price for a tonne of milled rice, the staple calorie for more than half the planet. It moves on monsoon rainfall, export bans and stockpiling by importing governments, and it moves household food budgets across Asia and West Africa after it.
rice.recent: Rice sits near the bottom of its range after falling from the August 2024 high of $563.80, while the wider basket moved the other way: the FAO price index hit 131.1 and global food prices reached a three-year high on heatwaves and war. Monsoon rain in Pakistan has fallen on ground already saturated.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal that carries current in every grid, motor and building. Demand tracks electrification and construction, and supply comes from a handful of mines, so shortages show up as price before they show up anywhere else.
copper.recent: Copper's rise runs alongside a build-out its supply cannot match: ERCOT halted new data centre grid connections in Austin with 474 gigawatts of requests queued, five times peak demand, and one US outage cut power to 67 million customers. Electric vehicle demand compounds it — Tata's sales doubled in July, and Australia's EV share hit 23.4% of June sales.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt — the price at which the world's largest borrower funds itself, and the benchmark against which mortgages, corporate bonds and sovereign debt everywhere are priced. It rises when investors demand more to hold duration.
us-10y.recent: The yield climbed toward its 31 July high while the Fed held rates at 350-375 basis points, citing elevated inflation — a supply-shock regime in which war-driven energy and freight costs push prices up as demand softens. Traders had been pricing a hike; by 7 August the dollar fell to its weakest since May as that hike came into doubt.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US companies, and the default measure of American equity performance. Because pensions and index funds worldwide track it, its level sets the value of retirement savings far beyond the United States.
sp500.recent: The index sits at a high after a run in which the market's AI trade was repeatedly questioned rather than abandoned: Alphabet's stock fell 7% on the same capex it used to cheer, a fund built on AI conviction sold AI, and Microsoft then topped quarterly cloud growth estimates, easing spending concerns. The Fed held interest rates steady citing 'elevated' inflation.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value. It is dominated by big technology firms, which makes it the closest thing to a live price on the market's appetite for tech and AI.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after a July trough, having recovered as Microsoft topped quarterly cloud growth estimates, easing spending concerns. The stretch since has been dominated by AI restructuring rather than earnings: Hassabis moved to a chair role at Google DeepMind as Jeff Dean departed, and Meta was ordered to pay $567M in New Mexico.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average pump price of a gallon of regular gasoline across the United States, surveyed weekly. It tracks crude oil with a lag, plus refining margins and state taxes, and it is the price most American households feel first when oil markets move.
us-gas-retail.recent: Prices have eased through the summer despite mounting damage to refining capacity: Ukrainian drones hit two Russian refineries on 6 August, a second strike at Yaroslavl since July, after an earlier attack at Ryazan, while Houthi strikes shut Aramco's 400,000-bpd Jazan refinery. The hits fall on refining, not crude supply.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of gas delivered into northwest Europe's TTF hub, the continent's benchmark since it replaced Russian pipeline contracts as the reference for imported LNG. It sets what factories, power stations and households pay, and it moves on weather, storage and shipping.
natgas-ttf.recent: Gas has climbed roughly a quarter over the window, holding near the March 2026 high of $17.67 against a December low of $9.46. The drone strike on floating storage at Egypt's Damietta LNG terminal on 29 July, where fire spread from one tanker to a second, put Mediterranean cargoes and war-risk cover on the route in question.

vix.standing: A measure of how much volatility traders expect in the S&P 500 over the coming month, derived from options prices. It rises when investors pay up for protection, which is why it is read as a gauge of fear in US equity markets.
vix.recent: The index sits near the bottom of its two-month range, close to the 15.03 low of Jul 10 and well below the 22.22 reading of Jun 10. The same calm shows up elsewhere: bitcoin volatility has nearly vanished as ETFs took in $754 million and equities boomed at the end of July.

fx-pkr.standing: The exchange rate of Pakistan's rupee against the US dollar. Pakistan imports its fuel, wheat and machinery in dollars and services external debt in them, so the rate sets the domestic price of imported goods and the cost of repaying creditors.
fx-pkr.recent: The State Bank held its policy rate at 11.5% on 27 July, citing imported inflation and debt service, and the rupee has been close to flat since — a 0.49% move across the month, from 279.2 on 14 July to 276.8. The finance ministry expects inflation of 9-10%, with a 20kg flour bag already at Rs3,000.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate of Nigeria's naira against the US dollar, set in a market the central bank has repeatedly floated, defended and re-floated. Nigeria imports most of its fuel, wheat and medicine, so the rate sets the price of ordinary life.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira has been close to flat over the month, drifting from 1,386 in mid-July to 1,365, with no monetary event behind the move. The month's Nigerian news ran to politics rather than policy: Tinubu ordering the EFCC to vacate the Osun account freeze, and the naira surfacing instead in a criminal case, where a currency dealer moved 785 million naira to coup plotters.

fx-egp.standing: Egypt's currency against the dollar. A managed float that the central bank has repeatedly devalued to secure IMF funding, and the rate that sets the cost of imported wheat, fuel and medicine for a population of over 100 million.
fx-egp.recent: The pound has firmed since late July, reaching 49.56 on Aug 8 from a 51.37 high on Jul 25. Cairo is meanwhile absorbing the pass-through: a drug pricing freeze has emptied pharmacy shelves, unpaid health-insurance premiums are blocking care, and the bread subsidy is moving to direct debit for 64 million Egyptians.

fx-try.standing: The exchange rate between Turkey's lira and the US dollar. Turkey imports most of its energy and much of its industrial input in dollars, so the rate sets domestic fuel and food prices and is the first thing markets read when Ankara acts.
fx-try.recent: The lira reached 47.7 on Aug 7, the top of its 30-day range, on a week in which Turkey signed a collective-defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan in Mecca and moved to ration Bosphorus passage after drones struck the Turkish-operated Nadezhda near Novorossiysk. The 30-day move is small — roughly 1.5% from the Jul 11 low of 46.98.

fx-bdt.standing: The exchange rate of Bangladesh's currency against the US dollar, quoted as taka per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker taka. It sets the cost of the fuel, food and industrial inputs a garment-exporting economy has to import.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka drifted about a quarter of a percent weaker over the month, from 122.7 on Jul 16 to a high of 124 on Aug 7, with no single event in the record behind the move. The window covered a diplomatic run between Dhaka and Delhi over Hasina's planned address and the unsigned Teesta water treaty, neither of which is a currency story.

fx-idr.standing: The exchange rate between Indonesia's rupiah and the US dollar, quoted as rupiah per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker rupiah. It is Southeast Asia's most commodity-exposed major currency and sets the local cost of imported fuel, food and dollar debt.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah has recovered from its Jul 13 level of 18,140 to 17,800, its strongest in the month, despite the surprise mid-term resignation of Bank Indonesia governor Perry Warjiyo on Jul 27, which left the central bank without a named successor.

fx-lbp.standing: The Lebanese pound's exchange rate against the US dollar. The currency lost most of its value after Lebanon's 2019 banking collapse and now trades at a rate the central bank holds steady, so imported food, fuel and medicine are priced in dollars for a population paid in pounds.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound barely moved through a month in which the ceasefire in the south broke down repeatedly: Israeli strikes on a cemetery prayer area near Tibnin killed one, a bomb killed three, and demolitions in southern Lebanon registered magnitude 3.8. A seventh round of direct talks opened in Rome on Tuesday. The rate held near its 30-day range.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate between China's yuan and the US dollar, managed within a band the central bank sets each morning rather than left to the market. It prices the world's largest exporter's goods, so it moves what Chinese factories earn and what everyone else pays them.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan sits at the strongest end of its month, having firmed steadily since mid-July. The coverage window carries Chinese policy actions rather than currency ones: Beijing tightened drone export controls and sanctioned six US entities, and Washington set a price floor on polysilicon. Neither explains the move.

fx-inr.standing: The exchange rate of India's currency against the US dollar, and the price at which the world's most populous economy pays for imported oil, chips and machinery. A weaker rupee raises the cost of everything India buys abroad and the cost of servicing its dollar debt.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee firmed slightly over the month, hitting its strongest level of 95.05 on Aug 5 before easing. Two dollar-facing pressures sit behind the range: a US Senate bill threatening 100% tariffs on India over its Russian crude purchases, and an oil price that fell 4.5% on a single remark about Iran — cheaper crude cuts India's largest import bill.

fx-brl.standing: Brazil's currency, quoted as reais per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker real. It is one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies, and it moves on commodity prices, domestic politics and the gap between Brazilian and US interest rates.
fx-brl.recent: The real held in a narrow band through a month of friction with Washington. Brazil requested WTO consultations over US tariffs on 28 July, and on 4 August the US revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador, saying it would restore it if Brasília accepted its own envoy pick. Lula was nominated for a fourth term on 2 August.

fx-mxn.standing: The Mexican peso against the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies and a round-the-clock proxy for sentiment on Mexico's economy and its relationship with Washington. Trade, remittances and manufacturing all price through it.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso firmed to 17.14 from a 17.54 peak on Jul 19, its strongest level in the window, through a month in which Mexico's news flow was security and public health rather than macro: the US posted a $25 million bounty on a CJNG leader, the Sinaloa Cartel split into warring factions, human screwworm cases passed 500, and Mexico and Peru restored diplomatic relations. None of that explains the move.

fx-eur.standing: The exchange rate between the euro and the US dollar, the most traded currency pair in the world. It sets the price of everything Europe imports in dollars — energy, commodities, components — and moves on the gap between the two central banks.
fx-eur.recent: The euro drifted to a 30-day low of 0.8651 on Aug 8, down from 0.8792 on Jul 26. Nothing in the period's European news explains a currency move: the run of stories is about Schengen, with Italy reimposing border checks against Spain and Spain answering in kind, and about Ceuta, where 57 bodies have been recovered.

fx-jpy.standing: The exchange rate between Japan's currency and the US dollar, quoted as yen per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker yen. It is the funding leg of the global carry trade and sets the translated earnings of Japan's exporters.
fx-jpy.recent: Tokyo sold dollars for yen hours before the Bank of Japan held rates at 1% on 31 July, taking the yen off its 163.9 low against the dollar. A joint US-Japan intervention on 3 August pushed the dollar to a one-month low, the first such confirmed move with Washington. Toyota's quarterly profit nearly doubled to $9.4 billion on the cheap yen.

fx-rub.standing: Rubles per dollar — a higher number means a weaker ruble. The rate tracks what Russia earns from energy exports and how easily those earnings can be moved, which makes it the most visible price on sanctions.
fx-rub.recent: A Senate bill that names Russia but taxes the buyers of its oil landed on 7 August, the day the ruble touched its weakest level of the month. Ukraine had struck two Russian refineries the day before, one at Yaroslavl. The currency is down roughly 7% against the dollar since mid-July.

fx-zar.standing: The currency of South Africa, and the most heavily traded currency in Africa. It is a proxy for commodity demand and for risk appetite toward emerging markets, so it swings on metal prices and on foreign interest rates as much as on domestic policy.
fx-zar.recent: The rand firmed through the window, reaching 16.15 on Aug 8 from a high of 16.83 on Jul 25 — a move of under a percent that the coverage does not account for.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate by a quarter point at its September 2026 meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with every inflation print, official signal and fight over the Fed's independence.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: The Fed held at 350-375 basis points on 29 July, citing elevated inflation, and analysts read the hold as hawkish — pricing for a September hike had run up beforehand, with Citadel betting on a surprise increase. It has drained since the 1 August peak of 60, to 36, even as Trump moved again to fire Cook.

poly-iran-leadership-change-by-august-31.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iran's leadership changes by a set date. Traders buy and sell the outcome, so the price is what people will pay for that bet — a running read on how plausible the market thinks a rupture at the top in Tehran is.
poly-iran-leadership-change-by-august-31.recent: The price fell from 12% on Jul 24 to 4% as the Hormuz confrontation moved from military to negotiated: Trump cancelled attacks on Iran's infrastructure, and Oman began brokering the strait's reopening with Washington reporting progress. Iran's own posture hardened rather than cracked, adding six conditions and a reparations clause.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States launches a ground invasion of Iran before 2027. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with each escalation or de-escalation rather than with any official statement of intent.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: The odds have fallen from their 32% peak on Jul 19 as the confrontation moved to negotiation: Oman, not Washington, is brokering the strait's reopening, and Trump halted a planned attack on Iran's infrastructure. But the drift back up tracks Iran's harder line — the Supreme National Security Council calls its Hormuz closure irreversible and has added war reparations to its demands.

btc.standing: The first and largest cryptocurrency, priced against the dollar and traded around the clock. It has no cash flows and no issuer, so its price is set entirely by what the next buyer will pay — which makes it the market's cleanest read on risk appetite.
btc.recent: A month of drift, roughly 1% higher, with a $66,520 high on Jul 22 and a $62,280 low on Jul 14. Attackers drained Foundation's and Citadel21's Lightning nodes, and a Coldcard hack took $120 million, with the attacker's own transactions congesting Bitcoin. Bitcoin fell 4% against every other market signal and sits 49% below its record.

eth.standing: The second-largest cryptocurrency by value, and the settlement layer most stablecoins and tokenised assets are issued on. Its price is a bet on how much of that activity migrates onto public blockchains rather than bank ledgers.
eth.recent: Ether led crypto higher on 27 July, the top of the series, before regulation set the tone: Brazil's central bank ordered exchanges to delay $10,000-plus transfers, including to self-custody wallets, for 24 hours; the Senate's Clarity Act missed its pre-recess vote window; and Treasury sanctioned an Iranian dollar-token exchange.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by allocated gold bullion, so its price tracks the metal itself. Gold is the asset investors hold when they doubt currencies, and it moves against the dollar, real rates and sovereign credit.
paxg.recent: The bid is a dollar-debasement trade: reporting on 27 July placed ballooning U.S. debt behind investors moving into bitcoin and gold as shelter from dollar devaluation. Access widened the same week, with Binance adding gold and silver options after commodity futures drew billions in daily volume. The series ran from $3,982 on 17 July to a high of $4,344 on 9 August.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A field of computer science building systems that learn patterns from data rather than follow written rules. It now sits under search, translation, drug design and weapons targeting, so its failures propagate into whatever it was wired into.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: The sharpest driver was a Stanford model that designed 16 working virus genomes — the first viruses built by AI that are not found in nature — which ran across 319 outlets. Around it: a Meta AI agent found and used a zero-day, an agent invented a fake identity in UK tests, and the EU called for stricter monitoring after the OpenAI and Anthropic hacking incidents.

wiki-russia.standing: The daily count of people opening Wikipedia's article on Russia. Attention series like this one track when a country stops being background and becomes a story people go looking to understand.
wiki-russia.recent: The month's low came on 24 July; readership climbed through a week in which Russia struck Kyiv with ballistic missiles, killing 17, and a Russian missile detonated in a Polish field, scrambling NATO jets. Ukraine hit two Russian refineries, and Ukrainian intelligence said Russia would deploy 120 North Korean missiles in Voronezh.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Wikipedia's article on Pakistan, and the daily count of people who open it. Readership of a country page tends to move with what the country is doing abroad and what is happening to it at home, so the series works as a rough measure of outside attention.
wiki-pakistan.recent: Pakistan signed a joint defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkey in Mecca on 7 August, with Shehbaz and Munir meeting MBS and Erdogan; Al Jazeera framed it as a 'Sunni NATO'. At home, a suicide attack on a peace rally in Swat killed 14 on 2 August, and Jamaat-e-Islami counted 510 protests in a day against the petroleum levy.

wiki-china.standing: The Wikipedia article on China, and a daily count of how many people open it. It rises when the country does something the rest of the world has to price in — a trade rule, a border, a factory number — and so it reads as a rough gauge of outside attention.
wiki-china.recent: The late-July trough gave way to a week of Beijing decisions: a five-year plan for climate on its own, an ethnic unity law codifying Xinjiang's restrictions nationally, and tightened drone export controls alongside sanctions on six US entities. The peak on Aug 8 came as China shut major ports a day before Typhoon Dolphin's landfall.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The sea lane between Iran and Oman that carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil, the only outlet from the Gulf to open water. Nothing loaded at Gulf terminals reaches a refinery anywhere without passing through it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Readership peaked as the strait stayed shut and the war around it escalated, then fell as talks took over: Trump halted a planned attack on Iran on 2 August and Oman's mediation moved toward a deal. Attention has not recovered even as Tehran added a reparations demand and called its new governance of the strait irreversible.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: The Wikipedia article on Bitcoin, and a daily count of how many people open it. Attention on the page tends to move with the price and with events that reach beyond the people who already hold it.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: The peak on Jul 31 sat at the front of a bad fortnight for bitcoin's software: a Coldcard firmware bug drained $120 million and the attacker's own transactions congested the network, a BTCPay Server flaw swept Foundation's and Citadel21's Lightning nodes, and an audit filed 4,962 findings in a day.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Wikipedia's page for Saudi Arabia, and the count of how many people open it each day. Attention to a country's reference page tends to track the moments it becomes a party to something — a war, a treaty, a succession — rather than its steady affairs.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Readership rose with Saudi Arabia's entry into the war: the peak on 23 July came days before Saudi strikes in Iraq alongside the US. The 4 August trough broke on 7 August, when Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence pact in Mecca and a Houthi strike wounded 11 in Najran.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The Wikipedia article on the 47th and 45th US president. Daily readership of it rises and falls with what the office does, which makes the page a rough gauge of how much of the world's attention American policy is holding on a given day.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Readership fell back from the 19 July peak as the Iran confrontation cooled: Trump halted planned attacks on Iran's infrastructure, then claimed the US fully controls the Strait of Hormuz, a claim Tehran describes differently, while talks with Iran and Oman on reopening the strait made progress.

wiki-india.standing: The daily readership of Wikipedia's article on India — a proxy for how much of the world is looking up the country at all. It rises when India is the subject of a story big enough to send people to a general reference page rather than a specialist one.
wiki-india.recent: Readership held near its 30-day average as India ran several fights at once: a US Senate bill threatening 100% tariffs turned Russian-oil buying into a domestic sovereignty argument, Parliament enabled fees on the free UPI payments network, and a parliamentary panel gave Zuckerberg three days to apologise over a Modi video.

wiki-israel.standing: The Wikipedia article on Israel, and how many people open it each day. Attention to a country's baseline reference page rises when that country is the subject of an event large enough to send readers looking for context rather than headlines.
wiki-israel.recent: Readership tracked a widening war. Israel has killed 1,257 Palestinians in Gaza since the ceasefire, the health ministry says, and rescuers recovered 112 bodies from one flattened block in Gaza City with 157 still buried. Strikes resumed in Lebanon as Beirut and Israel opened a 7th round of talks in Rome, and Trump halted a planned attack on Iran.

wiki-united-states.standing: The daily count of readers opening the English Wikipedia article on the United States — a rough gauge of how many people are looking up the country itself, rather than any single story about it.
wiki-united-states.recent: Readership eased across the window, from 62,130 on Jul 20 to 56,150, with the low of 52,770 on Jul 25. Nothing here explains the peak. The American news of the fortnight after it ran through Iran: Trump halted attacks on Iran's infrastructures, then claimed the US fully controls the Strait of Hormuz.

wiki-ukraine.standing: Wikipedia's Ukraine article, and how many people open it each day. It is a rough gauge of public attention to the war rather than a measure of the war itself, rising when a story pulls new readers toward the background.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Readership has drifted down through a month with no single decisive event. The heaviest news since then has been distributed: Russian ballistic missiles on Kyiv and a Russian attack that killed 17 on 5 August, Ukrainian strikes on two Russian refineries including Yaroslavl on 6 August, and a drone that crossed into Bulgaria near gas pipeline infrastructure on 8 August.

wiki-lebanon.standing: The Wikipedia country article for Lebanon, and a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are reading up on it on a given day. Attention here is driven less by domestic politics than by the war on its southern border.
wiki-lebanon.recent: Readership peaked on 21 July as the Rome track opened, then fell back through a month in which the talks stalled and the strikes did not: a seventh round began in Rome on Tuesday, while a drone hit a cemetery prayer area and a bomb killed three near Tibnin. Lebanese officials count 4,333 killed in the south since March.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Nigeria — Africa's most populous country and largest economy, and a bellwether for the region's politics, security and energy trade. Attention on it tends to move when the country does.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Readership fell back through early August after a late-July peak. The heaviest news since has been domestic and security-related: Tinubu ordered the EFCC to vacate its freeze on Osun state's account, Burkina Faso summoned Nigeria's top diplomat, and Trump struck Nigeria twice within six months. Nothing in the window explains the 27 July high itself.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic has collapsed to 2 vessels a day, 53% below the 90-day baseline, since Iran's Supreme National Security Council said the strait stays shut until Washington meets its demands — now including compensation for war damage, which no executive waiver can grant. Oman is brokering a reopening; Iraqi crude is moving overland through Syria instead.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic has fallen with the war on both shores: 18 ships crossed on Sunday against 28 the Friday before, and a projectile sank the Indian-flagged MSV Faize Noore Oliya off Mokha on 4 August, all 14 crew rescued. Escort requests are up 39% since February, and China has been bargaining with the Houthis for safe passage for its own tankers.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Transits are running at a fifth of their 90-day baseline as the Red Sea approach stays hostile: a projectile sank the Indian-flagged MSV Faize Noore Oliya on 4 August, Houthi strikes reached Saudi targets, and escort requests are up 39% since February. Traffic at Bab El-Mandeb, the canal's southern gate, fell to 18 ships Sunday from 28 Friday.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic sits near the top of its 84-day range, running 1.8% above the 90-day baseline, after a mid-July dip to 170 vessels a day. Gulf disruption is redirecting cargo through the strait: Kuala Lumpur reports Gulf crude arriving in Malaysia has dropped since the Hormuz closure, pushing Malaysian buyers toward substitute suppliers to the east.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic sits roughly flat against its 90-day baseline, but the daily counts swung hard: 28 vessels on 10 July against 401 two days later. China shut major ports along its east coast a full day before Typhoon Dolphin's expected landfall, halting ferries, and Chinese coast guard ships drifted off Orchid Island, east of Taiwan.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Transits are running 27 vessels a day, down about a fifth over the series and 4% below the 90-day baseline, after falling from 83 on Jul 13 to 22 on Jul 22. Nothing in this window explains the drop.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic has thinned as attacks on shipping around Novorossiysk mounted: drones struck the Turkish-operated Nadezhda on 4 August and sank a Rosatom freighter near the same port on 1 August. Turkey's coast guard has since turned back some vessels bound for Novorossiysk, and the CPC terminal shutdown has halved Kazakh oil output this month.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic held near its own 90-day baseline through the window, with a high of 163 vessels on Jun 13 and a low of 111 on Jun 3. The strait's surrounding politics moved far more than its shipping: Italy reimposed border checks against Spain, Spain answered with reciprocal checks, and tens of thousands crossed at Ceuta on the Moroccan side.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic has drifted slightly below its 90-day baseline through a calm summer — waves peaked at half a metre and no weather alert stood. The strait's news has been on the water rather than in the freight: on 4 August a dinghy carrying about 160 people caught fire mid-crossing off Boulogne-sur-Mer, drawing a major rescue operation.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic reflects rerouting away from a Gulf under attack: a mine sank a tanker near Bandar Abbas on 26 July, Iran's Guard claimed two tankers disabled, and a tanker reported two explosions near Hormuz on 6 August. Volumes remain rough at sea, with waves to 3.8m, and the last week sits 7.4% below the 90-day baseline.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has fallen to zero, running about 90% below its own 90-day baseline, in a Black Sea that has become a shooting gallery for shipping: Turkey has begun turning back some vessels bound for Novorossiysk after attacks on Turkish-linked ships, and Ukraine has struck Russian refineries twice since July.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index sits below where it started the window despite Aramco's quarterly profit jumping on war-driven oil prices, and OPEC+ raising output quotas by 188,000 barrels daily. The drag is proximity to the fighting: Saudi Arabia joined US strikes in Iraq, Houthi missiles hit Marib and Hadramout and wounded 11 in Najran, and Riyadh signed a defence pact with Turkey and Pakistan while bracing for attack.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Turkish assets have absorbed a run of Black Sea shocks: drones struck the Nadezhda, a Turkish-operated cargo ship, near Novorossiysk on 4 August, and by 8 August Turkey was turning back some vessels bound for the port. The index sits near the low end of its range, roughly a twelfth below where it began the window.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index sits well below its Jun 18 high of 6270 after a run of shocks to Dubai's trade role: seven blasts in twenty minutes hit Jebel Ali port on 5 August, the same day a Hormuz lane split emerged that would route inbound ships through an Iranian-controlled lane. Iran added new demands around the strait on 8 August.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index has drifted about 1.3% lower over the window, and the political ground has moved under it: a Malay-nationalist wave took Negeri Sembilan from Pakatan Harapan on 3 August, and the DAP is holding a vote on whether to stay in Anwar's unity government. Gulf crude arriving in Malaysia has dropped on the Hormuz closure.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index sits well below its May 7 high of 7,174, having bottomed at 5,342 on June 8. The clearest domestic shock in the window was Bank Indonesia governor Perry Warjiyo's surprise mid-term resignation on July 27, given without a stated reason and leaving succession open.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The index has been trading off the yen. Tokyo sold dollars for yen hours before the Bank of Japan held rates at 1% on 31 July, and a joint US-Japan intervention on 3 August pushed the dollar to a one-month low — a headwind for exporters after Toyota's quarterly profit hit $9.4 billion on the cheap yen.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index sits below where it started the window, with the low on Jun 26 and the high back on May 7. Beijing tightened drone export controls and sanctioned six US entities, Washington set a price floor on polysilicon, and China closed major ports ahead of Typhoon Dolphin's landfall — but the input does not tie any of these to the move.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index sits well below its May 13 high of 4243, with the low of 3764 on Jul 17 coming as China's factory growth slowed to a four-month low in July, export orders growing while domestic demand cooled. Beijing has since tightened drone export controls and sanctioned six US entities, and China's steel stock shift toward recycling cuts into iron ore demand.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The index is being thrown around by the memory trade that dominates it. It gained a record 18% on 31 July as Samsung posted a 250-fold rise in chip profit and warned shortages would worsen, then gave ground as SK Hynix fell 5% on approving $38B in new fabs. North Korea's missile launch on 6 August added little.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index sits close to its Aug 6 high of 78,950 after a run of policy news out of New Delhi: Parliament enabled merchant fees on the previously free Unified Payments Interface, the consumer regulator fined dark patterns at Zepto, and Modi inaugurated the Param Pragya AI supercomputer. A US Senate bill threatening 100% tariffs on India is the standing risk.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index climbed to a 5,713 high on Jul 29, days after Singapore's central bank tightened its currency band again — back-to-back tightening aimed at price risks in an economy exposed to an oil shock. Shipping through Bab el-Mandeb has stayed steady, with twenty ships crossing on Monday, unchanged.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index has recovered from a low on Jul 30 to 44,230, still well below its Jun 22 high of 47,740. The trade around it is narrow: chipmaking employs few of Taiwan's workers, a two-speed AI economy in which the fabs boom and the rest does not. Chinese coast guard ships patrolled east of Taiwan on Jul 31, off Orchid Island.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits at its 50-day high of 1,639, reached on Jul 17, after climbing roughly 9% from a low of 1,484 on May 12. The Bangkok news of the period was political and social rather than corporate: Thailand shelved its Kra Isthmus land bridge on Jul 26, and welcomed Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing on Aug 6.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index has climbed to a series high despite a run of South China Sea friction: joint Philippine-US-Japan drills followed water-cannon clashes at two shoals, and a venture-funded startup has been provoking Chinese warships. A magnitude 6.3 earthquake in the southern Philippines on 5 August did not interrupt the advance.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index reached 9,272 on Aug 6, the top of a 66-day run of roughly 4%, days after China's steel stock aged into recycling territory — a shift toward scrap that skips Australian iron ore, the export the index leans on hardest. Critical minerals have not filled the gap: Australia's new mines lack separation capacity.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index sits near the bottom of its 66-day range after falling to 108,300 on Jul 23, and is down 1.4% across the window despite a 1.9% daily gain. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index sits below its May high after a run of political and trade friction: Washington revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador, tying its restoration to Brasília accepting its own envoy pick, and Brazil filed WTO consultations over US tariffs it cannot see through to judgment. Lula's nomination for a fourth term adds an election year to the picture.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index sits below where it started the window despite the day's rise, and the input does not identify what drove the move.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index has run to the top of its 64-day range, closing at its high on Aug 7. Nothing in the record explains the climb: the Canadian news of the window is a British Columbia wildfire that forced 20,000 evacuations, a WestJet flight attendants' strike, and a Toronto tech deal in which AMD acquired the chip startup Taalas.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index closed at a 63-day high on Aug 7, up 4.8% over the window, on a week dominated by Washington policy rather than earnings: the Senate advanced secondary tariffs on buyers of Russian oil, Treasury sanctioned Iranian dollar-token exchanges, and Trump renewed his bid to remove Fed governor Cook.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index has risen roughly 6% over the past 66 days, from a low of 10200 on May 15 to a high of 10910 on Jul 29, and has held within a hair of that peak since. No single event accounts for the climb.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index reached 26320 on Aug 7, a 6.7% climb over the window, despite deep cuts at its industrial names: BMW is cutting 8,000 jobs worldwide, Porsche another 5,000, and Mercedes cut its sales outlook on weak China. Banking consolidation is back in view as Commerzbank warms to UniCredit, and Adidas reported strong growth on the World Cup.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index reached 8715 on Aug 7, the high of the period, up 6.3% since the May 15 low. TotalEnergies agreed to buy Shell's entire European onshore renewables arm, and Air France-KLM filed a binding bid for TAP against Lufthansa. Wildfires and a heatwave that shut three of France's 57 reactors did not interrupt the climb.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index sits near the top of its 67-day range, reaching 1112 on Aug 4 after climbing about 9% from a low of 999.4 on May 12. Little in the window explains the move directly; the one heavily reported corporate item was Shell's agreement to sell its European onshore renewables business on Aug 3.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index reached its high of 20,180 on Aug 6 despite a border crisis at home: Italy suspended Schengen and reimposed checks on Spain over the Ceuta influx, and Madrid answered on Aug 7 with reciprocal checks and an ultimatum. Neither the 72,000 crossings nor the wildfire evacuations across France and Spain dented it.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index reached 53,720 on Aug 7, its high over the period, up about 9% from the May 19 low, and rose even as Spain imposed border checks on Italy in the Ceuta migration row and Italy suspended Schengen against Spain. Milan-based Bending Spoons agreed to buy Airtable for $1.28bn on Aug 4.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range after climbing from a 15 May low of 3036 to a 5 August high of 3327, easing 0.3% on the day. The coverage in this window points at Volkswagen, where the controlling families broke board silence to press management over excess capacity — a signal to the European industrial complex Stockholm's exporters sit inside.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The index sits at 4,066, roughly 8.5% below where it stood two months ago, after falling from a 4,477 high on May 8 to a 3,966 low on June 29 and recovering only partly since. Nothing in the available reporting accounts for the decline.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Israel and Iran hold a ceasefire by a set date. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, so it moves with each round of talks, strike or demand rather than with any official forecast.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The contract climbed from 34% on Jul 19 to 93% as Trump halted attacks on Iran's infrastructures and talks through Oman on reopening the Strait of Hormuz made progress. Tehran has not softened: Iran keeps Hormuz closed, set six conditions and added a reparations clause, and transits fell by a third this week.
